prompt: A windup penguin moves along the $x$-axis with acceleration given by $a(t)=2t-2$ units per second$^2$. At $t=1$ second, the penguin is moving left with a speed of 4 units per second. What is the total distance the penguin travels in the first four seconds ($t=0$ to $t=4$)?

solutions.title: Integrate the speed
solutions.body:
$v(t)=t^2-2t+C$ and $v(1)=-4$ gives $C=-3$, so $v=(t-3)(t+1)$, negative on $[0,3)$ and positive on $(3,4]$. Distance $=-\int_0^3v\,dt+\int_3^4v\,dt=9+\frac73=\frac{34}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{34}3$**

prompt: The function $f(x)=\begin{cases}2+x^3,&x\le1\\3x,&x>1\end{cases}$ is differentiable on $(-1,2)$ and continuous on $[-1,2]$, and hence satisfies the hypotheses for the Mean Value Theorem on the interval $[-1,2]$. Find a value of $x$ which is guaranteed to exist by the theorem.

solutions.title: Apply the MVT
solutions.body:
The average slope is $\frac{f(2)-f(-1)}{3}=\frac{6-1}3=\frac53$. For $x>1$, $f'(x)=3\ne\frac53$. For $x\le1$, $f'(x)=3x^2=\frac53$ gives $x=\pm\frac{\sqrt5}3$; both lie in $(-1,1)$. Either value works.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt5}3$ (or $-\frac{\sqrt5}3$)**

prompt: Consider a function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$. Given that $f(0)=0$, $\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(h)}h=7$, and $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+3xy$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$, what is $f(7)$?

solutions.title: Direct
solutions.body:
Let $g(x)=f(x)-\frac32x^2$. Then $g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y)$ and $g'(0)=7$, so $g(x)=7x$ (additive and differentiable). Hence $f(7)=\frac{147}2+49=\frac{245}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{245}2$**

prompt:
A group of college students gets together to write math questions while eating cake. Teena eats $c(t)$ pieces of cake per hour and writes $q(t)$ questions per hour. The faster Teena eats cake, the less she wants to eat, so $c'(t)=-c(t)$. However, as she eats, she gets sleepy and writes questions more slowly, so $q'(t)=-3c(t)$.

When the question writing session begins (at $t=0$), Teena is writing 7 questions per hour and eating 2 pieces of cake per hour. But if she ever writes questions more slowly than 2 per hour, she gets kicked out. The question writing session lasts for 24 hours and thus ends at $t=24$. Does Teena get kicked out of the question writing session before it ends? And if so, when?

solutions.title: Solve the ODEs
solutions.body:
$c'=-c$ with $c(0)=2$ gives $c=2e^{-t}$. Then $q'=-6e^{-t}$, so $q=6e^{-t}+k$, and $q(0)=7$ gives $k=1$: $q(t)=6e^{-t}+1$. This decreases toward 1, so it drops below 2 when $6e^{-t}=1$, i.e. $t=\ln6$.

**Answer: Yes, after $\ln6$ hours**

solutions.title: Logarithmic differentiation
solutions.body:
Let $y=x^{x^x}$. Then $\ln y=x^x\ln x$, so $\frac{y'}y=(x^x)'\ln x+\frac{x^x}x$. Since $x^x=e^{x\ln x}$, $(x^x)'=x^x(\ln x+1)$. Hence $y'=x^{x^x}\cdot x^x\left((\ln x+1)\ln x+\frac1x\right)=x^{x^x+x}\left((\ln x)^2+\ln x+\frac1x\right)$.

**Answer: $x^{x^x+x}\left((\ln x)^2+\ln x+\frac1x\right)$**

prompt: Let $s>0$. Consider straight lines drawn from $(0,r)$ to $(s-r,0)$ for all $0\le r\le s$. We define $f(x)$ as the maximum $y$-value that any of these lines take on at $x$. Find $f(x)$ for $0\le x\le s$.

solutions.title: Maximise over r
solutions.body:
At $x$, the line with parameter $r$ (defined when $x\le s-r$) has height $g(r)=r\left(1-\frac x{s-r}\right)$ for $0\le r\le s-x$. Setting $g'(r)=0$: $(s-r)^2-x(s-r)-xr=0$, i.e. $r^2-2sr+s(s-x)=0$, so $r=s-\sqrt{sx}$ (the root $s+\sqrt{sx}$ is too large). This is a maximum ($g(0)=g(s-x)=0$, $g\ge0$). Then $f(x)=(s-\sqrt{sx})\left(1-\frac x{\sqrt{sx}}\right)=\sqrt s(\sqrt s-\sqrt x)\cdot\frac{\sqrt s-\sqrt x}{\sqrt s}=(\sqrt s-\sqrt x)^2$.

**Answer: $(\sqrt s-\sqrt x)^2$**

prompt: An hourglass (a shape composed of two cones of the same size joined at the apex oriented so that the hourglass sits on one of the cones' base) has a maximal radius of 12 inches and a total height of 10 inches. The sand inside occupies one-fourth of the total volume of the hourglass, and it takes one minute for all the sand to drop from the top cone to the bottom one (the hourglass is a one minute timer). Assuming the sand falls at a constant rate, what is the rate of change in the height of the sand in the bottom cone 15 seconds before the timer runs out? Assume the surface of the sand in the bottom cone is always flat.

solutions.title: Related rates
solutions.body:
Each cone has radius 12 and height 5; the hourglass has volume $2\cdot\frac13\pi\cdot144\cdot5=480\pi$, so the sand has volume $120\pi$ and falls at $\frac{dV}{dt}=2\pi$ in$^3$/s. Fifteen seconds before the end, $90\pi$ in$^3$ is in the bottom cone. Let $h$ be the sand's height and $r$ the radius of its top surface; by similar triangles $h=5-\frac{5r}{12}$. The empty part of the bottom cone is a cone of height $\frac{5r}{12}$ and radius $r$, so $V=240\pi-\frac{5\pi r^3}{36}$. When $V=90\pi$: $r^3=1080$, $r=6\sqrt[3]5$. Differentiating, $\frac{dr}{dt}=-\frac{24}{5r^2}$ and $\frac{dh}{dt}=-\frac5{12}\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac2{r^2}=\frac2{36\sqrt[3]{25}}=\frac{\sqrt[3]5}{90}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt[3]5}{90}$ inches per second**

prompt: Sammy the Owl is making a one-eyed Jack'o'Lantern. He bought a perfectly spherical pumpkin of radius 1 foot. He first carves out the inside so that the inner radius is 10 inches. He then drills a perfectly circular hole of radius 1 inch for the eye. He drills straight toward the center of the pumpkin at the "equator." What is the total volume in cubic inches of pumpkin that he has removed?

solutions.title: Cavity plus drilled shell
solutions.body:
The cavity has volume $\frac43\pi10^3=\frac{4000\pi}3$. The hole removes the part of the shell (between radii 10 and 12) inside the cylinder $\rho\le1$ about the drilling axis. The part of a ball of radius $R$ inside this cylinder on one side of the centre has volume $\int_0^12\pi\rho\sqrt{R^2-\rho^2}\,d\rho=\frac{2\pi}3\left(R^3-(R^2-1)^{3/2}\right)$. For $R=12$: $\frac{2\pi}3(1728-143\sqrt{143})$. For $R=10$: $\frac{2\pi}3(1000-297\sqrt{11})$. Subtracting gives the drilled shell volume $\frac{2\pi}3(728-143\sqrt{143}+297\sqrt{11})$. Adding the cavity: $\frac{5456\pi}3+198\sqrt{11}\pi-\frac{286\sqrt{143}\pi}3\approx4195.1$ in$^3$.

**Answer: $\frac{5456\pi}3+198\sqrt{11}\pi-\frac{286\sqrt{143}\pi}3$ cubic inches**
